rules.justification: Standard clinical threshold for diagnosing hypertension is a systolic blood pressure of 140 mmHg or higher.
The provided value represents systolic pressure; a value of 140 mmHg or higher is the clinical definition of elevated systolic blood pressure.
Total cholesterol levels of 200 mg/dl or higher are generally considered indicative of hypercholesterolemia.
Tachycardia is clinically defined as a heart rate exceeding 100 beats per minute.
Bradycardia is clinically defined as a heart rate below 60 beats per minute.
ST segment depression is clinically significant when it reaches 1 mm or greater.
The presence of any major vessels colored by fluoroscopy indicates coronary artery stenosis/disease.
The categorical values 'typical' and 'atypical' angina directly map to the phenotype Angina pectoris.
All types of pain listed in the chest_pain_type column represent a clinical presentation of chest pain.
A fasting blood sugar over 120 mg/dl is a clinical marker for hyperglycemia.
In clinical practice, fasting blood sugar levels over 120 mg/dl are frequently used as a screening threshold for diabetes mellitus.
Direct mapping of the 'left ventricular hypertrophy' categorical value.
An ST-T abnormality is a specific form of an abnormal EKG (electrocardiogram).
Presence of exercise-induced angina is a direct clinical finding for Angina pectoris.
A downsloping ST segment is a clinical finding associated with ST segment depression.
A downsloping ST segment is a type of abnormal ST segment morphology.
A flat ST segment during exercise is a clinical finding indicative of an abnormal ST segment.
